content.title: About
content.content: Wasabi peas are roasted green peas coated with a spicy blend of wasabi powder, salt, and sometimes soy sauce. They have a crunchy texture, bright green color, and a distinctive hot‑sharp flavor reminiscent of Japanese wasabi.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The peas used are typically sweet green peas, not the larger field peas.
Commercial wasabi seasoning is often made from horseradish because true wasabi (Wasabia japonica) is expensive and rare.
Wasabi peas are popular as a snack in Asian markets, convenience stores, and movie theaters.
Low‑sodium versions are available because the standard seasoning can be quite salty.
The crunchy peas retain most of the protein and fiber of the original legume.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Peas contain about 20 % protein, making wasabi peas a good source of plant‑based protein for a snack.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Unlike many nut‑based snacks, wasabi peas are low in fat, resulting in fewer calories per serving.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Peas provide thiamine (B1) and folate, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant properties of wasabi
items.content: Isothiocyanates such as piperine in wasabi have antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory effects.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salty versions can contain up to 400 mg of sodium per 30 g serving, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: People allergic to legumes (peas, beans) may react to wasabi peas.

items.title: Spicy seasoning
items.content: Excessive consumption can irritate the stomach in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Glutamate content
items.content: Some brands add soy sauce, which contains monosodium glutamate that can affect those with sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wasabi peas are convenient as a stand‑alone snack, tossed into salads, rice bowls, or used as a crunchy topping for soups and Asian dishes. They also pair well with dried fruit for a sweet‑spicy mix.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct light. For longer shelf life, store in the refrigerator to preserve crunch and flavor. Discard if they develop a stale or rancid smell or lose their crispness.
